judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001) is ALREADY in research.json — the orchestrator ran locality-guide before research-plan. The skill should READ that entry and use its quirks; it should NOT call wiki_search / wiki_place_page / place_population (research-plan does not hold those tools). Do NOT fail it for not surveying.

The quirk under test is loc_001's: "Norwegian name spellings were set by the recorder and vary between records (the wiki's example: the given name Sivert written as Syver, Sjur, Siver, Sifuer or Siffuer) — search given-name spelling variants, not just the tree's spelling, before concluding a nil. (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records)"

The persisted `plan_items[].rationale` is the only place that counts — narration is not persisted and search-records never sees it. Correctness turns on the plan item that searches the Norway marriage index (collection 1468080) for Unna: its persisted rationale must state that given-name spellings vary by recorder, so the search must try spelling variants of 'Unna', not only the exact spelling. A plan whose reply mentions the quirk while that item's rationale does not fails this point. Paraphrase is fine.
Plan items must include rationale explaining why each record type was chosen for the question — generic rationale ('more records would help') is a fail.
